assessments.title: Financial foundations and goals: Inflation in Imani Workshop (sponsored-view 1-all-1)
assessments.description: Apply Distinguish needs from wants, set measurable goals, and understand how inflation and compounding change purchasing power. to a inflation decision at Imani Workshop. Work with stated KSh amounts and periods, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and explain why the selected method fits.
learning_objectives: Explain how inflation relates to financial foundations and goals.
Calculate or interpret a financial measure using explicit units and assumptions.
Identify a risk, limitation, or ethical consideration before acting on the result.

questions.prompt: In the case titled "Financial foundations and goals: Inflation in Imani Workshop (sponsored-view 1-all-1)," calculate budget balance. Income is 6,401 KSh and planned outgoings are 689 KSh. What amount remains after those outgoings?
questions.rationale: Budget balance = income minus planned outgoings = 6,401 minus 689 = 5,712.00 KSh. A positive result is planned headroom, not proof cash has arrived.

questions.prompt: A planning note from Imani Workshop gives these amounts. Income for the period is 6,640 KSh and the amount set aside is 820 KSh. What percentage of income is saved?
questions.rationale: Savings rate = savings divided by income, multiplied by 100 = 820 divided by 6,640 divided by 100 = 12.35%; total income is the denominator.

questions.prompt: Use the stated assumptions for Imani Workshop; ignore fees not specified. A basket costs 6,879 KSh today. At 12% annual inflation, what is its estimated cost one year later?
questions.rationale: Estimated one-year cost = current cost multiplied by (1 + inflation rate) = 6,879 multiplied by (1 + 12/100) = 7,704.48 KSh. Rounded to the nearest KSh, the selected answer is 7,704 KSh.

questions.prompt: Imani Workshop is the setting for this one-year compound growth check. A deposit of 7,118 KSh earns 15% interest compounded annually. What is its balance after one year, before fees and tax?
questions.rationale: One-year balance = principal multiplied by (1 + annual rate) = 7,118 multiplied by (1 + 15/100) = 8,185.70 KSh before fees and tax. Rounded to the nearest KSh, the selected answer is 8,186 KSh.

questions.prompt: A repair-shop manager at Imani Workshop records the following figures. An emergency reserve is 7,357 KSh and essential monthly costs are 1,213 KSh. How many months of costs does it cover?
questions.rationale: Reserve coverage = reserve divided by essential monthly costs = 7,357 divided by 1,213 = 6.07 months.

questions.prompt: In the case titled "Financial foundations and goals: Inflation in Imani Workshop (sponsored-view 1-all-1)," which response best addresses ethical financial conduct? A manager finds that a forecast omits a likely cost and the omission benefits the manager's bonus. What is the most responsible next step?
options: Disclose the omitted cost, correct the forecast, and document the change.
Keep the omission because a forecast is only an estimate.
Move the cost to an unrelated account to protect the bonus.
Wait until after the bonus is paid before informing anyone.
questions.correct_answer: Disclose the omitted cost, correct the forecast, and document the change.
questions.rationale: Transparent correction prevents a misleading forecast; documenting the change creates an audit trail and addresses rather than conceals the conflict.

questions.prompt: A planning note from Imani Workshop gives these amounts. Opening cash is 7,835 KSh, receipts are 1,475 KSh, and payments are 343 KSh. What is closing cash?

questions.prompt: Imani Workshop is the setting for this inflation-adjusted cost check. A basket costs 8,313 KSh today. At 14% annual inflation, what is its estimated cost one year later?

questions.prompt: In the case titled "Financial foundations and goals: Inflation in Imani Workshop (sponsored-view 1-all-1)," which response best addresses diversification? An investor holds nearly all savings in one employer's shares. Which action most directly reduces company-specific concentration risk?
options: Spread exposure across investments with different issuers and risk drivers.
Buy more shares of the same employer to lower the average purchase price.
Borrow to increase the position in the employer.
Ignore concentration because the employer also pays a salary.
questions.correct_answer: Spread exposure across investments with different issuers and risk drivers.
questions.rationale: Different issuers and risk drivers can reduce company-specific concentration, although diversification cannot eliminate market-wide losses.
